role: Bounded architectural development; no promotion or confirmatory claims
seedUnit: Four familiar underlying level-8 seed blocks, crossed with four policies; sixteen worlds are not sixteen independent weeks.
arms: portfolio plus future value and payment choices
stopping: Complete all 16 worlds regardless of profit. A runtime, solver-bridge, unneutralized deadline or 600-second world-budget failure stops new creation, preserves all partial artifacts and lets other running worlds finish. Portfolio network failures abort rather than reconstruct incomplete reservations. Control retains its existing transient recovery. Five-minute occupancy wait. No mid-panel tuning or favorable interim stopping.

data.offline: Original 57 training/19 model-test seed split from the 76 familiar weeks. Pre-quote logistic booking, drop and lateness priors use original request fields; no award-only or reveal feature. Only booking/lateness priors enter decisions; drop model is diagnostic.
data.online: Existing customer-choice updates; fully matured 120-minute booking cohorts with 12 pseudo-orders, canceled cohorts censored. Same starting models every week. No payment-response fitting during play.

planner.candidates: At most three earliest-response unquoted requests and six owned single-car anchors per decision, at most 120 candidates. Held orders take priority; open anchors within 70km fill remaining slots. At most two best feasible anchors per request. No open/open route rewrites, no two-uncertain-request pair, no trade-in/private-address expansion. Mandatory keep/decline alternatives preserve all modeled commitments. Overflow held work uses the inherited solo post and is logged.
planner.quotes: The inherited safety/eligibility/deadline checks generate legal options, with scalar count gates broadened during proposal generation; joint resource constraints enforce bounded admission. Offer all those options at one ratio. For each route/payment strategy, recompute a logistic-optimal price from modeled marginal fulfillment, refund, penalty and future costs, then compare that ratio and +/-4%, plus the incumbent ratio. Levels below 4 retain the actual first-option rule, but this panel is level 8 only.
planner.objective: Expected delivered customer revenue minus fulfillment, refunds and undelivered penalties plus future value. Existing anchors carry their full continuation economics even when the new customer declines. Baseline and alternative both include anchor revenue once. Shared route savings capped at 15% of modeled cost. Route lateness odds approximated by a 15% probability increase; this is an assumption, not a fitted causal effect.
planner.scenarios: Eight common parameter scenarios: customer normalized-price shifts +/-0.04, early-booking probability shifts +/-0.05, payment-response slopes 0 or 4. Customer wins are integrated analytically within each scenario. Shared capacity reserves p+0.5*sqrt(p*(1-p)), capped at 1; this is not a hard guarantee for simultaneous wins. Open-anchor survival derives from its modeled 120-minute booking probability over time to quote resolution. Held anchors are reserved only until the pending quote resolves.
planner.costRisk: Fulfillment starts at max(current opening fee, baseFee*1.15). Early-booking probability uses the logistic prior plus half the local matured-cohort deviation from the pooled prior, bounded [0.05,0.99]. Higher payment changes expected fee and booking risk under the declared sensitivity slopes. Refund severity is 40% of price conditional on delivered lateness. Undelivery probability is 2% of modeled lateness, capped at 2%; subtract missing revenue and charge twice-price penalty. These tail assumptions are deliberately explicit and unvalidated.
planner.resources: Separate geographic daily and unbooked-work constraints by ready day. Nearby work weighs 1 within30km, 0.5 within70km. Original daily/backlog capacities retain a 1.5x upper envelope. Acquired anchors are removed from outside load and included once in each candidate. Existing baseline commitments remain feasible even if already beyond the cap.
planner.qualificationRisk: Sum modeled lateness probabilities in 1/10000-order units under every parameter scenario. Available risk is 0.06*(20+won orders) minus observed late deliveries and modeled outstanding/pending risk, floored at the mandatory baseline. Booked outside work receives0.3 of its original lateness risk. This is a model-based constraint, not a certified qualification-probability bound.
planner.futureValue: One terminal capacity/positioning term only. Estimate positive contribution per work minute from at most20 nearby requests observed in the last180minutes, using1.1x public list prices minus expected cost; cap40c/min and scale by observed utilization above0.5. Positioning reduces the charge by at most20%. No additional overlapping scarcity charge or learned state-value model.
planner.payments: Only the opening fee changes, choosing100% or108% with escalation preserved and fees monotone. The two-week randomized data do not identify a reliable causal curve; slopes0/4 are frozen sensitivity assumptions. No extra direct-offer mechanism in this panel.
planner.execution: Execute one selected quote/post/withdrawal, then advance and replan. Initial neutral declines protect quote deadlines; remove the queued neutral decline when a real quote is sent. Successful withdrawal moves the anchor to held work; the next solve decides its route. Refused withdrawals preserve both commitments. Rescue actions remain inherited. Log every solver input, candidate action, output and actual result.
planner.solver: OR-Tools9.11.4210, one worker, fixed seed170114,0.2-second solve budget and3-second bridge budget. Verify baseline independently; no feasible solver answer returns baseline. Record status and bound, never call a feasible incumbent optimal. All dependencies and source files frozen by manifest.

analysis: All paired net profits, qualification, orders, driver payments, refunds, fines, undelivered orders, failed visits, action errors and runtime failures retained. Reconcile score to all ledger lines. Descriptive paired-t and whole-week bootstrap intervals; exact qualification lower bounds under IID assumptions. Report solver fallback, omissions and action types. Four adaptive blocks cannot support confirmation.
validation: No untouched seeds or alpha allocation. A passing arm only nominates one finalist for a new frozen paired evaluation; minimum24 unique pairs, increased for meaningful effect, variance and reliability. The current 95% qualification target at first allocated alpha needs86 zero-failure pairs. No ranking without explicit permission.
knownLimits: Booked changed routes cannot gain a charging stop through the API; fines and charging-risk logs remain in outcomes.
Observed home supply is not guaranteed capacity. Parameter scenarios and fractional reservations do not capture every joint tail.
Scoring assumes additive outcomes except shared claims/resources. Future driver learning and nonlinear competition between selected plans remain approximate.
Wall-clock solver limits can alter feasible incumbents; all realized decisions are retained.
